subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output requirements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output requirements

Alex — thanks for your time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we have alignment. TL;DR: you're looking to power parts of your customer support workflow with agent-driven actions and deterministic structured outputs (JSON) for downstream systems.

Key pain points we heard
- Current bot returns freeform text that downstream systems (ticketing, billing) can’t reliably parse.
- Manual handoffs are frequent because the assistant can’t take deterministic actions (create/update tickets, return structured billing adjustments).
- Risk/QA team needs strict schema validation and reproducible outputs (no hallucinated fields).

Current stack
- Front end: React web chat (Proprietary)
- Orchestration: internal microservice that ingests assistant responses and maps to workflows
- Data sources: CRM (Salesforce), internal ticketing API, billing databases

Success criteria you called out
1) Agent can call a function/tool to perform an action (create_ticket, lookup_invoice, propose_credit) and return a deterministic JSON payload that our orchestration service can consume without additional NL parsing.
2) JSON schema is validated on every response; any deviation fails the workflow and surfaces for human review.
3) Low false-positive action invocation (we need clear confidence / guardrail strategy).
4) Response formatting must be stable across repeated calls (determinism for same input).

Proposed approach & POC scope
- Define a small canonical JSON schema for 3 actions: create_ticket, lookup_invoice, propose_credit (attached example-json-schema.json).
- Implement function/tool calling in POC with Redwood: tool call returns both an action invocation record and a structured JSON response.
- Add deterministic formatting tests: run same prompt + context 10x, require >=95% exact-match on required fields and types.
- Acceptance: your orchestration service ingests POC responses without additional parsing and successfully creates/updates tickets in staging.

Next steps
1) I’ll share the discovery deck and a small example schema (attached).
2) You (Alex) will confirm the list of required fields for each action and any additional non-negotiable validation rules by EOD next Tue (2026-03-10).
3) Schedule a short technical sync to map our tool definitions to your ticketing API (30–45m).

Attachments: discovery-deck.pdf (slides), example-json-schema.json

Thanks again — happy to iterate on the schema.

Best,
Jordan Blake

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>

Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output requirements

Thanks Jordan — this is great and matches my notes. A few clarifications and additions: 

Clarifications
- On determinism: we don't require bitwise identical output for every token, but the JSON object must be byte-for-byte identical for required fields and types when the same input/context is provided. Minor ordering differences are OK only if you can guarantee our parser accepts them.
- Confidence thresholds: for action invocations we want a confidence score and an allow/deny policy. If confidence < 0.85, the system should escalate to a human-in-the-loop.

Additions
- For lookup_invoice we need an optional field invoice_source ("payments_db" | "third_party_gateway"). If lookup fails, the tool should return a standardized error code (e.g., INVOICE_NOT_FOUND) and a structured reason.
- Our security team requires audit logs for all tool calls including full request/response and user id.

We can confirm required fields for the 3 actions; I'll send our list by Mon (2026-03-09).

Quick ask: can you include a simple example of how Redwood returns tool-call results in the response envelope? An example snippet in the POC schema would help our engineers map the response to our ingestion layer.

Alex
Alex Morgan
Director, Customer Experience
Acme Financials

Appreciate the clarifications, Alex — super helpful. Attached is a minimal example of the response envelope we typically produce for a tool call (see example-json-schema.json). Short excerpt from the attached for quick reference:

--- begin excerpt ---
{
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "create_ticket",
    "confidence": 0.92,
    "payload": {
      "ticket_id": "TKT-12345",
      "priority": "high",
      "summary": "User reported incorrect billing charge"
    },
    "error_code": null
  },
  "raw_text": "Please create a ticket for billing error..."
}
--- end excerpt ---

Notes on determinism and testing
- We'll implement a schema validation layer that runs on every response and returns a pass/fail status.
- For POC stability tests we'll run repeated calls (same seed/context) and record exact-match rates on payload objects.
- We can also return a normalized canonical form (sorted keys, deterministic serialization) if you prefer to avoid parser-level ordering issues.

Next steps (updated)
- Jordan: send POC environment details and the example schema (done, attached).
- Alex: confirm required fields + any additional error codes by Mon 2026-03-09.
- Set up a 30m technical mapping call next week. I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue/Wed.

If it helps, Rachel can run a short internal smoke test against your staging ticketing API once we agree on the field names.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

Jordan
